newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt to start land use study group - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt to start land use study group - spokesman.

text.p: Japan's government will set up a study group comprised of several cabinet ministers to study ways to promote the effective use of land in the nation's sluggish real estate market, Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama said on Friday.
Kajiyama told a news conference that the group would map out specific measures within six months on city redevelopment, alignment of land plots and securitisation of real estate.

The study group will consist of the finance, justice, construction and home affairs ministers, chiefs of the national land and economic planning agencies, the chief and deputy chief cabinet secretaries and policy-makers from the ruling Liberal Democratic Party and two other parties which support it in a loose alliance.

The government is expected to announce on Monday a set of measures to boost liquidity in the land market in an effort to help financial firms burdened with problem loans, many of which are backed by property as collateral.
Included in the steps will be plans to permit the securitisation of commercial property used as loan collateral.
Analysts have said the measures expected to be announced are a useful first step towards boosting property market liquidity, but will not go all the way to solve the problems.

Separately, a Construction Ministry official said on Friday that the ministry plans to abolish the minimum size requirement for plots of land which can be bought by the Organisation for Promoting Urban Development (OPUD). The OPUD is a private entity which receives some public money.
The official said that he expected the measure to be included in the overall package to be unveiled on Monday.
